Every verified entry now records BOTH numbers, as runtime_ms.cold and runtime_ms.warm in verified-queries.yaml, cold being wall time through this route on that sweep; the header of that file says exactly what was and was not measured. SO, ON A TIMEOUT: resubmit the SAME SQL once, with retryOf, BEFORE changing anything. If the second call also times out, that is a real cost signal rather than a cold cache — narrow the question then (a year floor, a tighter applicant or CPC anchor, an aggregate instead of a row listing) and never send the identical SQL a third time. FIRST CHECK WHICH CHANNEL YOU ARE ON, because on one of them the resend has already happened: the FlowLeap CLI resends ANY 5xx automatically, twice, 250 ms and 500 ms apart (client.rs send_retrying, FLOWLEAP_MAX_RETRIES, silent unless you pass -v), so a 504 that reaches you through `flowleap patstat query` is the THIRD identical failure and the retry is spent — narrow it, do not send it again. A slow SUCCESS on that channel is the same mechanism showing its other face: a 34 s wall time on a 20 s statement timeout is a cold attempt that failed and a warm one that worked, not a query that ran for 34 s. Over raw HTTP (/v1/patstat/query direct) nothing retries for you and the one identical resend is yours to make. Synonyms users say: company, assignee, owner, holder, firm.","application":"One request for patent protection at one office. The unit of counting for office-level statistics.","extended family":"INPADOC extended family — every application linked to the same first filing DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY, including through examiner-judged technical relations and continuations. WIDER than a family: in the data catalog's own words it \"covers one or more DOCDB families and covers a set of RELATED inventions\". Use it to answer where a right is alive; never to count inventions. Synonyms users say: INPADOC family, extended patent family.","family":"All applications worldwide covering the same invention (DOCDB simple family). (CONTEXT.md canonical term; see global_caveats.psn_harmonization for what it does NOT collapse)","industry sector":"A NACE Rev. 2 manufacturing industry the TECHNOLOGY of a filing maps to (flowleap.sectors), derived from the filing's IPC symbols. (CONTEXT.md canonical term)","person entity":"One harmonized person or organisation, identified by psn_id — the KEY behind the harmonized name, exposed on applicants and inventors. A name is what a user says; psn_id is what an entity IS, and the two are not interchangeable because psn_name is not unique (203 of 195,839 sampled names carry more than one psn_id; 'WANG, Yu' is four different people). Match by name, then carry psn_id; group and join on psn_id, never on a name string. It does NOT make identity exact — it inherits the harmonization, so one company can still be two psn_ids (global_caveats.psn_harmonization).","portfolio":"Aggregate view of one applicant's activity. Layer 1's patstat_applicant_ambiguous 422 stays a Layer-1 feature.","query_errors":"ONE OF THE GATE ERRORS IS WORTH RESUBMITTING UNCHANGED, AND ONLY ONE. patstat_sql_timeout (504) is RETRY-WORTHY, and it is the exception — a COLD TIMEOUT rather than a heavy query: these views read tables far larger than the database cache (tls231_inpadoc_legal_event 122 GB, tls215_citn_categ 113 GB, tls203_appln_abstr 96 GB against 32 GB of shared buffers), so a first call can pay a disk read on every probe while the IDENTICAL query, sent straight back with those pages still resident, often finishes well inside the 20 s limit. Measured 2026-09-16 on patstat_2026_spring through /v1/patstat/query: the verified entry ep_oppositions_by_year returned patstat_sql_timeout cold and succeeded on an immediate retry, and portfolio_by_year_office took 20.0 s cold against 1.8 s warm — same SQL, same edition, nothing changed but the cache. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-17 AFTER A DELIBERATE DATABASE RESTART, AND THAT CLIFF IS GONE: all 34 verified entries ran cold without a single timeout, the slowest at 5.1 s, ep_oppositions_by_year at 4.5 s and portfolio_by_year_office at 4.5 s — the visibility-map VACUUM, the narrowing of three entries and the pinned planner statistics each contributed. Every verified entry now records BOTH numbers, as runtime_ms.cold and runtime_ms.warm in verified-queries.yaml, cold being wall time through this route on that sweep; the header of that file says exactly what was and was not measured. THE RETRY IS STILL THE RIGHT FIRST MOVE — these tables are still far larger than the cache and the mechanism has not changed — but treat a cold timeout as the exception now rather than the expected first call, and when you quote an entry's runtime to a user, say WHICH of the two numbers you are quoting. SO, ON A TIMEOUT: resubmit the SAME SQL once, with retryOf, BEFORE changing anything. If the second call also times out, that is a real cost signal rather than a cold cache — narrow the question then (a year floor, a tighter applicant or CPC anchor, an aggregate instead of a row listing) and never send the identical SQL a third time. FIRST CHECK WHICH CHANNEL YOU ARE ON, because on one of them the resend has already happened: the FlowLeap CLI resends ANY 5xx automatically, twice, 250 ms and 500 ms apart (client.rs send_retrying, FLOWLEAP_MAX_RETRIES, silent unless you pass -v), so a 504 that reaches you through `flowleap patstat query` is the THIRD identical failure and the retry is spent — narrow it, do not send it again. A slow SUCCESS on that channel is the same mechanism showing its other face: a 34 s wall time on a 20 s statement timeout is a cold attempt that failed and a warm one that worked, not a query that ran for 34 s. Over raw HTTP (/v1/patstat/query direct) nothing retries for you and the one identical resend is yours to make. THE OTHER SQL ERRORS ARE THE OPPOSITE, so do not treat this as a general retry licence: patstat_sql_forbidden (403), patstat_sql_too_expensive (422), patstat_sql_invalid (400) and patstat_sql_error (400) each say the SQL itself must change, and an unchanged resubmission fails identically while spending the 10-per-minute budget. THREE OF THE 503s ARE NOT ABOUT YOUR SQL AT ALL, and they are different from each other. patstat_busy (503) is LOAD: every guarded-SQL slot is taken, so keep the SQL exactly as it is and wait out the Retry-After delay. patstat_unreachable (503) is an OUTAGE: the PATSTAT database, the tunnel to it or the connection pooler is down or restarting, NOTHING is wrong with your SQL, and rewriting it cannot help — honour Retry-After and resend the SAME query, and if it is still failing after a couple of rounds say so plainly rather than inventing a narrower question. patstat_unavailable (503) is PERMANENT for this deployment: PATSTAT was never configured here, so no retry will ever work and you should answer from the document layer (the EPO/USPTO tools) or tell the user the analytics surface is not available. SAY WHICH ONE HAPPENED when you report back: `it timed out twice, so I bounded it to 2010 onwards` is a result the user can judge; `the query failed` is not.","when_to_ask":"Interrupt the user BEFORE generating SQL only when reasonable interpretations diverge materially (e.g. 'top applicant' by inventions vs by filings changes the ranking). content.text: The docs mention a verified example named ep_oppositions_by_year. I'll fetch the examples and the legal_events view definition together.

{"attribution":"This product contains data sourced from EPO databases, © European Patent Organisation","data_edition":"PATSTAT 2026 Spring","examples":[{"caveats":["Call patstat_portfolio (POST /v1/patstat/portfolio) instead of running this SQL: it resolves the entity, refuses an ambiguous name with the candidates, nulls unreliable grant counts (WO, ES, PL) and quotes the edition. This SQL is the same scope written out, for when you must extend it.","SCOPE IS ONE HARMONIZED ENTITY, NOT A NAME PREFIX. A bare `UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'SIEMENS%'` over-counts: it also counts sibling entities, for example the SIEMENS HEALTHCARE, SIEMENS MOBILITY, SIEMENS ENERGY and SIEMENS GAMESA RENEWABLE ENERGY groups. Measured 2026-09-30 on patstat_2026_spring for 2016-2026: 68,965 applications for the bare prefix against 32,497 for the endpoint's entity, 2.1 times more. Keep the regexp_replace equality, and replace 'SIEMENS' in it with the entity key: the name in upper case, `.` and `,` removed, and trailing legal forms such as AG, GMBH, CORP or LTD removed.","Resolve first when the name is not a single entity: SELECT ap.name, COUNT(DISTINCT ap.application_id) FROM flowleap.applicants ap WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'X%' GROUP BY ap.name ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 15 (interpretation_conventions.entity_disambiguation). Several different keys in that list are several entities: ask which one, never add them together.","This SQL returns 32,503 applications, 6 more than the endpoint's 32,497, one each in six year-office cells. The endpoint groups only the 200 largest names that match the prefix, so it misses rare spellings of the same entity (SIEMENS COMPANY, SIEMENS LTD., SIEMENS CORP). Quote the endpoint's number.","`granted` here counts every office. The endpoint reports WO, ES and PL grants as null and leaves them out of its totals, so this column is higher (9,288 against the endpoint's 8,281 for 2016-2026)."],"logical_sql":"SELECT a.office, a.filing_year,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) AS applications,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.granted THEN a.application_id END) AS granted
FROM flowleap.applications a
JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'SIEMENS%'
  AND regexp_replace(
        btrim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(UPPER(ap.name), '[.,]', ' ', 'g'), '\s+', ' ', 'g')),
        '( (CORPORATION|CORP|INCORPORATED|INC|COMPANY|CO|LIMITED|LTD|LLC|LLP|PLC|AKTIENGESELLSCHAFT|AG|GMBH|MBH|KGAA|KG|OHG|UG|SE|SA|SAS|SARL|SRL|SPA|NV|BV|AB|AS|APS|OY|OYJ|KK|KABUSHIKI|KAISHA))+$', '') = 'SIEMENS'
  AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2016 AND 2026 AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
GROUP BY a.office, a.filing_year
ORDER BY a.filing_year, applications DESC
","promoted_to":"POST /v1/patstat/portfolio (Layer 1, shipped)","question":"Show me {applicant}'s worldwide patent filing activity by year and office."},{"logical_sql":"SELECT ap.name, COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id) AS families,
       MIN(a.earliest_filing_year) AS active_since
FROM flowleap.classifications c
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = c.application_id
JOIN flowleap.applicants ap  ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/0562%' AND a.earliest_filing_year >= 2015
GROUP BY ap.name ORDER BY families DESC LIMIT 15
","promoted_to":"planned: POST /v1/patstat/landscape","question":"Who dominates {technology_area}? (top applicants by invention count)"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT a.earliest_filing_year AS filing_year, a.office,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id) AS families
FROM flowleap.classifications c
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = c.application_id
WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/056%'
  AND a.earliest_filing_year BETWEEN 2010 AND 2025
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC
","promoted_to":"planned: POST /v1/patstat/trends","question":"How fast is {technology_area} growing, and in which offices?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH fam AS (
  SELECT a.family_id, MAX(a.citing_families) AS citing_families_attr
  FROM flowleap.publications p
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = p.application_id
  WHERE p.office = 'EP' AND p.number = '2771468'
  GROUP BY a.family_id)
SELECT f.family_id, f.citing_families_attr,
       COUNT(DISTINCT fc.citing_family_id) AS citing_families_counted
FROM fam f LEFT JOIN flowleap.family_citations fc ON fc.cited_family_id = f.family_id
GROUP BY 1, 2
","promoted_to":"planned: POST /v1/patstat/citations","question":"How influential is the {publication} patent family?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT COUNT(*) AS citing_documents,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.is_x) AS x_cited,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.is_y) AS y_cited,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.is_a) AS a_cited,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.categories IS NULL) AS uncategorized,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.origins LIKE '%SEA%' OR cr.origins LIKE '%ISR%'
                           OR cr.origins LIKE '%SUP%' OR cr.origins LIKE '%EXA%'
                           OR cr.origins LIKE '%PRS%') AS examiner_found
FROM flowleap.citations_received cr
JOIN flowleap.publications fp ON fp.publication_id = cr.cited_publication_id
WHERE fp.application_id IN (
  SELECT fm.application_id
  FROM flowleap.family_members fm
  WHERE fm.family_id = (
    SELECT a.family_id
    FROM flowleap.publications p
    JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = p.application_id
    WHERE p.office = 'EP' AND p.number = '2771468'
    LIMIT 1))
","question":"How often is {publication}'s family cited as novelty-destroying (X) or inventive-step (Y) art?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT fm.office, COUNT(DISTINCT fm.application_id) AS applications,
       MIN(fm.filing_date) AS first_filing,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN fm.granted THEN fm.application_id END) AS granted
FROM flowleap.publications p
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = p.application_id
JOIN flowleap.family_members fm ON fm.family_id = a.family_id
WHERE p.office = 'EP' AND p.number = '2771468'
GROUP BY fm.office ORDER BY applications DESC
","promoted_to":"planned: POST /v1/patstat/family","question":"Where is the {publication} invention protected?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT le.event_office, le.event_code, COUNT(*) AS occurrences,
       MIN(le.event_date) AS first_seen, MAX(le.event_date) AS last_seen
FROM flowleap.legal_events le
WHERE le.application_id = (
  SELECT p.application_id
  FROM flowleap.publications p
  WHERE p.office = 'EP' AND p.number = '2771468'
  LIMIT 1)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY first_seen
","question":"What happened legally to {publication}?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT tf.sector, tf.field, COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id) AS families
FROM flowleap.applications a
JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
JOIN flowleap.tech_fields tf ON tf.application_id = a.application_id
WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'SIEMENS%' AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2015 AND 2024
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY families DESC LIMIT 10
","question":"What technology fields is {applicant} active in?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT i.name AS inventor, COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id) AS families
FROM flowleap.applications a
JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
JOIN flowleap.inventors i   ON i.application_id = a.application_id
WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'SIEMENS%' AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2015 AND 2024
GROUP BY i.name ORDER BY families DESC LIMIT 10
","question":"Who are {applicant}'s most prolific inventors on filings from {year} to {year}?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT symbol, level, title
FROM flowleap.cpc_scheme
WHERE title ILIKE '%photovoltaic%' AND (level IS NULL OR level = 0)
ORDER BY symbol LIMIT 20
","question":"Which CPC codes cover {technology_term}? (verify/find codes before landscaping)"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT a.office, COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) AS applications,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.granted THEN a.application_id END)
                   / COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id), 1) AS grant_rate_pct
FROM flowleap.classifications c
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = c.application_id
WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/056%'
  AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2010 AND 2018 AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
  AND a.office <> 'WO'
GROUP BY a.office HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) >= 100
ORDER BY grant_rate_pct DESC
","question":"Where is it easiest to get a {technology_area} patent granted?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT 'priority'::text AS relation, pr.priority_seq AS seq,
       anc.application_id, anc.office, anc.filing_date, anc.granted
FROM flowleap.priorities pr
JOIN flowleap.applications anc ON anc.application_id = pr.priority_application_id
WHERE pr.application_id = 414237564
UNION ALL
SELECT co.link_kind, NULL::smallint, anc.application_id, anc.office, anc.filing_date, anc.granted
FROM flowleap.continuations co
JOIN flowleap.applications anc ON anc.application_id = co.parent_application_id
WHERE co.application_id = 414237564
ORDER BY 5, 2
","question":"What does {application} claim priority from, and what is it a continuation or divisional of?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH hop1 AS (
  SELECT pr.application_id, 'priority'::text AS link
  FROM flowleap.priorities pr
  WHERE pr.priority_application_id = 905384508
  UNION
  SELECT co.application_id, co.link_kind
  FROM flowleap.continuations co
  WHERE co.parent_application_id = 905384508
), hop2 AS (
  SELECT pr.application_id, 'priority'::text AS link
  FROM flowleap.priorities pr
  JOIN hop1 h ON h.application_id = pr.priority_application_id
  UNION
  SELECT co.application_id, co.link_kind
  FROM flowleap.continuations co
  JOIN hop1 h ON h.application_id = co.parent_application_id
), descent AS (
  SELECT e.application_id,
         MIN(e.hop) AS hop,
         string_agg(DISTINCT e.link, ',' ORDER BY e.link) AS reached_via
  FROM (SELECT application_id, link, 1 AS hop FROM hop1
        UNION ALL
        SELECT application_id, link, 2 AS hop FROM hop2) e
  GROUP BY e.application_id
)
SELECT d.hop, d.reached_via, a.office,
       COUNT(*) AS applications,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id) AS families
FROM descent d
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = d.application_id
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY 1, 4 DESC
","question":"What has descended from {application} — everything claiming priority from it or continuing it — within 2 hops?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT ap.name AS applicant, a.filing_year,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) AS applications,

","question":"Which {office} legal-event codes mean {concept}?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH grants AS (

","question":"How many of {applicant}'s EP grants filed since {year} were opposed, by year?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH grants AS (

","question":"In which states does {applicant} let its EP patents lapse, and when?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH hits AS (

","promoted_to":"none","question":"IPC landscape for {ipc_prefix} by year and office."},{"logical_sql":"WITH corpus AS (

FROM flowleap.legal_events le
WHERE le.application_id = (
  SELECT p.application_id
  FROM flowleap.publications p
  WHERE p.office = 'EP' AND p.number = '2771468'
  LIMIT 1)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY first_seen
","question":"What happened legally to {publication}?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT tf.sector, tf.field, COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id) AS families
FROM flowleap.applications a
JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
JOIN flowleap.tech_fields tf ON tf.application_id = a.application_id
WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'SIEMENS%' AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2015 AND 2024
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY families DESC LIMIT 10
","question":"What technology fields is {applicant} active in?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT i.name AS inventor, COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id) AS families
FROM flowleap.applications a
JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
JOIN flowleap.inventors i   ON i.application_id = a.application_id
WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'SIEMENS%' AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2015 AND 2024
GROUP BY i.name ORDER BY families DESC LIMIT 10
","question":"Who are {applicant}'s most prolific inventors on filings from {year} to {year}?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT symbol, level, title
FROM flowleap.cpc_scheme
WHERE title ILIKE '%photovoltaic%' AND (level IS NULL OR level = 0)
ORDER BY symbol LIMIT 20
","question":"Which CPC codes cover {technology_term}? (verify/find codes before landscaping)"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT a.office, COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) AS applications,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.granted THEN a.application_id END)
                   / COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id), 1) AS grant_rate_pct
FROM flowleap.classifications c
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = c.application_id
WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/056%'
  AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2010 AND 2018 AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
  AND a.office <> 'WO'
GROUP BY a.office HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) >= 100
ORDER BY grant_rate_pct DESC
","question":"Where is it easiest to get a {technology_area} patent granted?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT 'priority'::text AS relation, pr.priority_seq AS seq,
       anc.application_id, anc.office, anc.filing_date, anc.granted
FROM flowleap.priorities pr
JOIN flowleap.applications anc ON anc.application_id = pr.priority_application_id
WHERE pr.application_id = 414237564
UNION ALL
SELECT co.link_kind, NULL::smallint, anc.application_id, anc.office, anc.filing_date, anc.granted
FROM flowleap.continuations co
JOIN flowleap.applications anc ON anc.application_id = co.parent_application_id
WHERE co.application_id = 414237564
ORDER BY 5, 2
","question":"What does {application} claim priority from, and what is it a continuation or divisional of?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH hop1 AS (
  SELECT pr.application_id, 'priority'::text AS link
  FROM flowleap.priorities pr
  WHERE pr.priority_application_id = 905384508
  UNION
  SELECT co.application_id, co.link_kind
  FROM flowleap.continuations co
  WHERE co.parent_application_id = 905384508
), hop2 AS (
  SELECT pr.application_id, 'priority'::text AS link
  FROM flowleap.priorities pr
  JOIN hop1 h ON h.application_id = pr.priority_application_id
  UNION
  SELECT co.application_id, co.link_kind
  FROM flowleap.continuations co
  JOIN hop1 h ON h.application_id = co.parent_application_id
), descent AS (
  SELECT e.application_id,
         MIN(e.hop) AS hop,
         string_agg(DISTINCT e.link, ',' ORDER BY e.link) AS reached_via
  FROM (SELECT application_id, link, 1 AS hop FROM hop1
        UNION ALL
        SELECT application_id, link, 2 AS hop FROM hop2) e
  GROUP BY e.application_id
)
SELECT d.hop, d.reached_via, a.office,
       COUNT(*) AS applications,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id) AS families
FROM descent d
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = d.application_id
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY 1, 4 DESC
","question":"What has descended from {application} — everything claiming priority from it or continuing it — within 2 hops?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT ap.name AS applicant, a.filing_year,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) AS applications,
       COUNT(DISTINCT co.application_id) AS divisionals,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT co.application_id)
                   / COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id), 1) AS divisional_share_pct
FROM flowleap.classifications c
JOIN flowleap.applications a  ON a.application_id = c.application_id
JOIN flowleap.applicants ap   ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
LEFT JOIN flowleap.continuations co
       ON co.application_id = a.application_id AND co.link_kind = 'divisional'
WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/056%'
  AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2010 AND 2022
  AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
GROUP BY 1, 2
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) >= 20
ORDER BY divisional_share_pct DESC, applications DESC
","question":"Who files the most divisionals in {technology_area}, as a share of their filings, by year?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT c.code, c.description, c.category, c.category_title
FROM flowleap.legal_event_codes c
WHERE c.office = 'EP'
  AND c.description ILIKE '%opposition%'
ORDER BY c.category NULLS LAST, c.code
","question":"Which {office} legal-event codes mean {concept}?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH grants AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id
  FROM flowleap.applications a
  JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
  WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'BASF%' AND a.office = 'EP' AND a.granted
    AND a.filing_year >= 2000
), opposed AS (
  SELECT le.application_id,
         MIN(le.event_date) AS first_opposition_date,
         COUNT(*)           AS opposition_event_rows
  FROM grants g
  JOIN flowleap.legal_events le ON le.application_id = g.application_id
  WHERE le.event_office = 'EP'
    AND le.event_code IN ('26', 'PLBI', 'R26')
    AND le.event_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY le.application_id
)
SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.first_opposition_date)::int AS opposition_year,
       COUNT(*)                       AS grants_opposed,
       SUM(o.opposition_event_rows)   AS event_rows
FROM opposed o
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
","question":"How many of {applicant}'s EP grants filed since {year} were opposed, by year?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH grants AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id
  FROM flowleap.applications a
  JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
  WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'BAYER%'
    AND a.office = 'EP' AND a.granted
    AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2015
)
SELECT le.lapse_country,
       EXTRACT(YEAR FROM le.lapse_date)::int      AS lapse_year,
       COUNT(DISTINCT le.application_id)          AS patents_lapsed
FROM grants g
JOIN flowleap.legal_events le ON le.application_id = g.application_id
WHERE le.event_office = 'EP'
  AND le.event_code IN ('PG25', 'VS25')
  AND le.lapse_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 2 DESC, 3 DESC
","question":"In which states does {applicant} let its EP patents lapse, and when?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH hits AS (
  SELECT tx.application_id
  FROM flowleap.application_texts tx
  WHERE to_tsvector('english', tx.title) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', 'solid state battery electrolyte')
    AND tx.title_lang = 'en'
), scoped AS (
  SELECT h.application_id, a.family_id
  FROM hits h
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = h.application_id
  WHERE a.ipr_type = 'PI' AND a.earliest_filing_year >= 2015
), codes AS (
  SELECT LEFT(c.cpc_code, 4) AS cpc_subclass,
         c.cpc_code,
         COUNT(DISTINCT s.family_id)      AS families,
         COUNT(DISTINCT s.application_id) AS applications
  FROM scoped s
  JOIN flowleap.classifications c ON c.application_id = s.application_id
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT k.cpc_subclass, k.cpc_code, k.families, k.applications,
       ROUND(100.0 * k.families / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT family_id) FROM scoped), 1) AS share_of_hits_pct,
       sub.title AS subclass_title, grp.title AS code_title
FROM codes k
LEFT JOIN flowleap.cpc_scheme sub ON sub.symbol = k.cpc_subclass
LEFT JOIN flowleap.cpc_scheme grp ON grp.symbol = k.cpc_code
ORDER BY k.families DESC, k.cpc_code
LIMIT 30
","question":"Which CPC codes dominate {concept} filings? (derive the codes from the corpus, not from a table)"},{"logical_sql":"WITH hits AS (
  SELECT tx.application_id
  FROM flowleap.application_texts tx
  WHERE to_tsvector('english', tx.abstract) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', 'solid state battery electrolyte')
    AND tx.abstract_lang = 'en'
), scoped AS (
  SELECT h.application_id, a.family_id
  FROM hits h
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = h.application_id
  WHERE a.ipr_type = 'PI' AND a.earliest_filing_year >= 2015
), codes AS (
  SELECT LEFT(c.cpc_code, 4) AS cpc_subclass,
         c.cpc_code,
         COUNT(DISTINCT s.family_id)      AS families,
         COUNT(DISTINCT s.application_id) AS applications
  FROM scoped s
  JOIN flowleap.classifications c ON c.application_id = s.application_id
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT k.cpc_subclass, k.cpc_code, k.families, k.applications,
       ROUND(100.0 * k.families / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT family_id) FROM scoped), 1) AS share_of_hits_pct,
       sub.title AS subclass_title, grp.title AS code_title
FROM codes k
LEFT JOIN flowleap.cpc_scheme sub ON sub.symbol = k.cpc_subclass
LEFT JOIN flowleap.cpc_scheme grp ON grp.symbol = k.cpc_code
ORDER BY k.families DESC, k.cpc_code
LIMIT 30
","question":"Which CPC codes dominate {concept} filings, matching the ABSTRACT for recall rather than the title for precision?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH hits AS (
  SELECT tx.application_id
  FROM flowleap.application_texts tx
  WHERE to_tsvector('english', tx.title) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', 'solid state battery electrolyte')
    AND tx.title_lang = 'en'
), scoped AS (
  SELECT h.application_id, a.family_id, a.office
  FROM hits h
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = h.application_id
  WHERE a.ipr_type = 'PI' AND a.earliest_filing_year >= 2015
)
SELECT ap.name AS applicant,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.family_id)      AS families,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.application_id) AS applications,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.office)         AS offices
FROM scoped s
JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = s.application_id
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.family_id) >= 5
ORDER BY families DESC, applicant
LIMIT 25
","question":"Who are the top applicants for {concept} since {year}?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH anchor AS (
  SELECT inpadoc_family_id
  FROM flowleap.inpadoc_family_members
  WHERE application_id = 16277555
)
SELECT m.office,
       COUNT(*)                          AS members,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE m.granted) AS granted_members,
       MIN(m.filing_date)                AS earliest_filing
FROM anchor a
JOIN flowleap.inpadoc_family_members m ON m.inpadoc_family_id = a.inpadoc_family_id
GROUP BY m.office
ORDER BY members DESC, m.office
","promoted_to":"none","question":"Where is the extended family of {application} alive — which offices, and how many of those members are granted?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH anchor AS (
  SELECT inpadoc_family_id
  FROM flowleap.inpadoc_family_members
  WHERE application_id = 16277555
)
SELECT COUNT(*)                     AS extended_members,
       COUNT(DISTINCT fm.family_id) AS docdb_families_inside,
       COUNT(DISTINCT m.office)     AS offices
FROM anchor a
JOIN flowleap.inpadoc_family_members m ON m.inpadoc_family_id = a.inpadoc_family_id
JOIN flowleap.family_members fm        ON fm.application_id = m.application_id
","promoted_to":"none","question":"How much wider is the extended family of {application} than its simple family — is it safe to count inventions over it?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT ipc.ipc_code,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id)      AS families,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) AS applications
FROM flowleap.applicants ap
JOIN flowleap.applications a          ON a.application_id = ap.application_id
JOIN flowleap.ipc_classifications ipc ON ipc.application_id = a.application_id
WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'ROBERT BOSCH%'
  AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
  AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2015 AND 2024
  AND ipc.ipc_value = 'invention'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY families DESC, ipc.ipc_code
LIMIT 25
","promoted_to":"none","question":"What technology does {applicant} file in, by IPC group?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT a.filing_year, a.office,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id) AS families
FROM flowleap.ipc_classifications ipc
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = ipc.application_id
WHERE ipc.ipc_code LIKE 'H01M10/056%'
  AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
  AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2015 AND 2024
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC
LIMIT 5000
","promoted_to":"none","question":"IPC landscape for {ipc_prefix} by year and office."},{"logical_sql":"WITH corpus AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id
  FROM flowleap.applicants ap
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = ap.application_id
  WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'ROBERT BOSCH%'
    AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
    AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2024
)
SELECT s.nace_code, s.nace_title,
       ROUND(SUM(s.weight), 1) AS weighted_applications,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(s.weight) / SUM(SUM(s.weight)) OVER (), 1) AS share_pct
FROM corpus c
JOIN flowleap.sectors s ON s.application_id = c.application_id
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY weighted_applications DESC
LIMIT 15
","promoted_to":"none","question":"Which industry sectors does {applicant} file in from {year} to {year}, and in what proportion?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH corpus AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id
  FROM flowleap.classifications c
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = c.application_id
  WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/0562%'
    AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
    AND a.earliest_filing_year >= 2015
)
SELECT s.nace_code, s.nace_title,
       ROUND(SUM(s.weight), 1) AS weighted_applications,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(s.weight) / SUM(SUM(s.weight)) OVER (), 1) AS share_pct
FROM corpus c
JOIN flowleap.sectors s ON s.application_id = c.application_id
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY weighted_applications DESC
LIMIT 12
","promoted_to":"none","question":"Which industries does {technology_area} belong to?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT r.nuts_code, r.nuts_label, r.nuts2_code, r.nuts2_label,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) AS applications,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id)      AS families
FROM flowleap.applicant_regions r
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = r.application_id
WHERE UPPER(r.applicant_name) LIKE 'ROBERT BOSCH%'
  AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
  AND a.filing_year BETWEEN 2015 AND 2024
  AND r.nuts_level IN (1, 2, 3, 4)
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
ORDER BY families DESC, r.nuts_code
LIMIT 15
","promoted_to":"none","question":"Where is {applicant} based — which regions do its filings come from?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH corpus AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id, a.family_id
  FROM flowleap.classifications c
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = c.application_id
  WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/0562%'
    AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
    AND a.earliest_filing_year >= 2015
)
SELECT r.nuts2_code, r.nuts2_label,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.family_id)      AS families,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.application_id) AS applications
FROM corpus c
JOIN flowleap.applicant_regions r ON r.application_id = c.application_id
WHERE r.nuts_level IN (3, 4)
  AND r.nuts_code LIKE 'DE%'
  AND r.nuts2_code IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY families DESC, r.nuts2_code
LIMIT 20
","promoted_to":"none","question":"Which {country} regions file in {technology_area} since {year}?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH corpus AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id, a.family_id
  FROM flowleap.classifications c
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = c.application_id
  WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/0562%'
    AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
    AND a.earliest_filing_year BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025
)
SELECT UPPER(REGEXP_REPLACE(n.journal_or_source, '[《》]', '', 'g')) AS source_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT n.cited_npl_id) AS citation_strings,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.family_id)    AS citing_families
FROM corpus c
JOIN flowleap.npl_citations n ON n.citing_application_id = c.application_id
WHERE n.npl_type = 'journal-article'
  AND n.journal_or_source IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY citing_families DESC, source_name
LIMIT 15
","promoted_to":"none","question":"Which journals and other literature sources do patents in {technology_area} cite, since {year}?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH corpus AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id, a.family_id, ap.name AS applicant
  FROM flowleap.classifications c
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = c.application_id
  JOIN flowleap.applicants ap  ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
  WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/0562%'
    AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
    AND a.earliest_filing_year BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025
)
SELECT c.applicant,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.family_id)    AS families,
       COUNT(n.cited_npl_id)          AS npl_citations,
       COUNT(DISTINCT n.cited_npl_id) AS citation_strings
FROM corpus c
JOIN flowleap.npl_citations n ON n.citing_application_id = c.application_id
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY npl_citations DESC, c.applicant
LIMIT 15
","promoted_to":"none","question":"Who cites the most non-patent literature in {technology_area}?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH corpus AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id, a.family_id
  FROM flowleap.classifications c
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = c.application_id
  WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/0562%'
    AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
    AND a.earliest_filing_year BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025
)
SELECT n.work_key,
       MIN(n.title)             AS title,
       MIN(n.journal_or_source) AS journal_or_source,
       MIN(n.publication_year)  AS publication_year,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.family_id)    AS citing_families,
       COUNT(DISTINCT n.cited_npl_id) AS citation_strings
FROM corpus c
JOIN flowleap.npl_citations n ON n.citing_application_id = c.application_id
WHERE n.npl_type = 'journal-article'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY citing_families DESC, n.work_key
LIMIT 15
","promoted_to":"none","question":"Which individual papers do patents in {technology_area} cite most?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH corpus AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id, a.earliest_filing_year AS filing_year
  FROM flowleap.classifications c
  JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = c.application_id
  JOIN flowleap.applicants ap  ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
  WHERE c.cpc_code LIKE 'H01M10/0562%'
    AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
    AND a.earliest_filing_year BETWEEN 2015 AND 2024
    AND UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'TOYOTA%'
), pubs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT p.publication_id, c.filing_year
  FROM corpus c
  JOIN flowleap.publications p ON p.application_id = c.application_id
), npl AS (
  SELECT pb.filing_year,
         COUNT(DISTINCT (n.citing_publication_id, n.cited_npl_id)) AS npl_references
  FROM pubs pb
  JOIN flowleap.npl_citations n ON n.citing_publication_id = pb.publication_id
  GROUP BY 1
), pat AS (
  SELECT pb.filing_year,
         COUNT(DISTINCT (r.citing_publication_id, r.cited_publication_id)) AS patent_references
  FROM pubs pb
  JOIN flowleap.citations_received r ON r.citing_publication_id = pb.publication_id
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT npl.filing_year, npl.npl_references, pat.patent_references,
       ROUND(100.0 * npl.npl_references
             / (npl.npl_references + pat.patent_references), 1) AS npl_share_pct
FROM npl
JOIN pat ON pat.filing_year = npl.filing_year
ORDER BY 1
","promoted_to":"none","question":"How much of what {applicant} cites in {technology_area} is literature rather than patents?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT w.npl_id, w.work_key, w.npl_type, w.journal_or_source,
       w.publication_year, w.xp_number, w.authors
FROM flowleap.npl_publications w
WHERE UPPER(w.doi) = UPPER('10.1126/science.1225829')
ORDER BY w.npl_id
LIMIT 200
","promoted_to":"none","question":"Which PATSTAT records correspond to the paper {doi}?"},{"logical_sql":"SELECT a.office,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id)      AS citing_families,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) AS citing_applications,
       MIN(a.earliest_filing_year)      AS first_year,
       MAX(a.earliest_filing_year)      AS last_year
FROM flowleap.npl_citations n
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = n.citing_application_id
WHERE n.cited_npl_id = ANY (ARRAY(
        SELECT w.npl_id FROM flowleap.npl_publications w
        WHERE UPPER(w.doi) = UPPER('10.1126/science.1225829')))
  AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY citing_families DESC, a.office
LIMIT 25
","promoted_to":"none","question":"Which patents cite the paper {doi}, and where were they filed?"}]}

A COARSE FILTER ONLY, NEVER a stand-in for a legal concept — EP category H mixes lapse with revocation, expiry, annulment and surrender. input.question: How many of Siemens's EP grants filed since 2015 were opposed, by year? Use PATSTAT.
input.sql:
WITH grants AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id
  FROM flowleap.applications a
  JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
  WHERE ap.psn_id = 30138991 AND a.office = 'EP' AND a.granted
    AND a.filing_year >= 2015 AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
), opposed AS (
  SELECT le.application_id,
         MIN(le.event_date) AS first_opposition_date,
         COUNT(*)           AS opposition_event_rows
  FROM grants g
  JOIN flowleap.legal_events le ON le.application_id = g.application_id
  WHERE le.event_office = 'EP'
    AND le.event_code IN ('26', 'PLBI', 'R26')
    AND le.event_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY le.application_id
)
SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.first_opposition_date)::int AS opposition_year,
       COUNT(*)                       AS grants_opposed,
       SUM(o.opposition_event_rows)   AS event_rows
FROM opposed o
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

input.question: How many of Siemens's EP grants filed since 2015 were opposed, by year? Use PATSTAT.
input.sql:
WITH grants AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.application_id, a.filing_year
  FROM flowleap.applications a
  JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
  WHERE ap.psn_id = 30138991 AND a.office = 'EP' AND a.granted
    AND a.filing_year >= 2015 AND a.ipr_type = 'PI'
), opposed AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT le.application_id
  FROM grants g
  JOIN flowleap.legal_events le ON le.application_id = g.application_id
  WHERE le.event_office = 'EP'
    AND le.event_code IN ('26', 'PLBI', 'R26')
    AND le.event_date IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT g.filing_year,
       COUNT(*) AS ep_grants,
       COUNT(o.application_id) AS grants_opposed,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(o.application_id) / COUNT(*), 1) AS opposed_pct
FROM grants g
LEFT JOIN opposed o ON o.application_id = g.application_id
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
